Register a Class as a Tree Node

Source: R/tree.R
register_tree_node.Rd

Makes the objects of a class nodes of a tree rather than leaves: flatten() and build_tree() recurse into the children flatten returns, unflatten() rebuilds an object of the class from them with unflatten, and tree_repr() (and so the tree's printer) renders the node with repr. This is JAX's register_pytree_node(), plus the printer.

Besides its children, flatten returns the object's aux data: whatever else unflatten needs to rebuild it, such as a setting that is not an array. The class and the aux data are part of the tree's structure, compared with identical(), so two trees that differ in either are not equal and the dispatcher compiles them separately. Keep the aux data small and put the arrays among the children.

An object is a node of the first of its classes that is registered. A registered class cannot be registered again: to change its functions, unregister it with unregister_tree_node() and register it anew. A tree keeps the registration it was built under: it unflattens and prints its objects with that registration's functions even after the class is unregistered, and it is not equal to a tree built under another registration of the class, so the dispatcher never serves an entry compiled under the old functions.

Usage

register_tree_node(class, flatten, unflatten, repr)

unregister_tree_node(class)

Arguments

class

(character(1))
The class.

flatten

(function)
Takes an object of the class and returns list(children, aux): its children, a bare list whose names the tree keeps, and its aux data, any value (NULL if there is none).

unflatten

(function)
Takes the children, a list named as flatten names them, and the aux data, and returns an object of the class.

repr

(function)
Takes the children's tree_repr() strings, a character vector named as flatten names the children, and the aux data, and returns the node's string, a character(1), which tree_repr() shows as it is. Render nodes that differ in their aux data or their children's names differently, so that trees that are not equal print differently.

Value

NULL, invisibly.

See also

flatten(), build_tree()

Examples

point <- function(x, y, unit) {
  structure(list(x = x, y = y, unit = unit), class = "point")
}
register_tree_node(
  "point",
  flatten = function(p) list(list(x = p$x, y = p$y), p$unit),
  unflatten = function(children, unit) point(children$x, children$y, unit),
  repr = function(children, unit) {
    sprintf("point[%s](%s)", unit, paste(children, collapse = ", "))
  }
)
flatten(list(point(1, 2, "cm"), 3))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] 3
#> 
tree <- build_tree(list(point(1, 2, "cm"), 3))
tree
#> list(point[cm](*, *), *)
unflatten(tree, list(10, 20, 30))
#> [[1]]
#> $x
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $unit
#> [1] "cm"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "point"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 30
#> 
build_tree(point(1, 2, "cm")) == build_tree(point(1, 2, "in"))
#> [1] FALSE
unregister_tree_node("point")
